clue.text: Speculator correct to avoid leftish tendency?

parts.note: a bear is a speculator who sells expecting prices to fall
correct as an adjective: right, not wrong

explanation.surface: A financial gambler is told to put things straight and keep clear of any left-wing leanings.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAR RIGHT is a driving or walking instruction; the question mark admits the definition is playful, since a drift to the left is what you steer away from.
explanation.definitionFit: Veering to the right is the instruction you follow when a car or path keeps pulling leftwards.

definitions.meaning: second meaning: The ..., the nickname of the Royal East Kent Regiment, a British army regiment

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as loyal camp followers of an army unit, but the second half names the unit itself: The Buffs, an old English infantry regiment named for its buff-coloured facings.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffs are devotees of a hobby, and The Buffs was the long-standing nickname of an English regiment.

clue.text: Continent containing men suffering from loss of memory

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the continent wraps round the other letters
suffering suggests the men are in a bad way, knocked out of their normal order

parts.note: the letters of men, rearranged
the largest continent

explanation.surface: A large region is home to men with memory problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Amnesia is the medical term for a partial or total loss of memory.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: status or position in a hierarchy
second meaning: a line of people or things

explanation.walkthrough: 'Standing row' looks like a line of people on their feet; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Rank means both social or military position and a line of soldiers or waiting taxis.

parts.note: G is one of the musical notes A to G
a rip is a tear in cloth

explanation.surface: Someone finds a letter torn inside a handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like it puts one thing inside another, but here it only links the wordplay to its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A grip, or gripsack, is an old word for a travelling bag.

clue.text: Story-book exhibition where people may be spotted

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT is the New Testament, the usual book of crosswords
a show is a display or exhibition

explanation.surface: A display of children's stories where the pictures are full of spotty characters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spotted' means noticed by talent scouts, not covered in spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A talent show is a contest where performers hope to be noticed by agents looking for new stars.

clue.text: Talk foolishly though right in the head

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, with right sitting within the head

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
R is the standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone babbles nonsense even though they are perfectly sane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right in the head' reads as the idiom for sane, but it is the instruction to put R inside a word for head.
explanation.definitionFit: To prate is to chatter idly and at length, an older verb for talking nonsense.

clue.text: Note about gentle flower providing natural source of energy

parts.note: prim means demure and mild-mannered, a loose match for gentle
E is one of the musical notes A to G
something that flows moves along, so a flower here is read as a thing in motion

explanation.surface: A message about a delicate bloom that turns out to be a power source in nature.
explanation.walkthrough: This parse is uncertain. The answer fits every crossing, but 'about' cannot be placing one piece around another, and the readings for 'gentle' and 'flower' are stretched. The newspaper text may have been misread.
explanation.definitionFit: A prime mover is the original force that sets things going, such as wind or water driving a machine.

clue.text: Eager desire to get rich from flogging caviare

indicators.note: flogging suggests beating something until it is knocked out of shape

parts.note: taken as written, the older spelling of caviar

explanation.surface: Someone hungers to make a fortune by selling expensive fish eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flogging' reads as selling, which suits the money-making surface; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Avarice is greed for wealth, an eager desire to become rich.

clue.text: Can perhaps last out with patience

indicators.note: perhaps hints that can is only one possible order of its letters
with here means holding alongside inside, so the word for last out takes the other letters within it

parts.note: to endure is to last out, to survive to the end
the letters of can, rearranged

explanation.surface: A tin can, maybe, survives for a long time with patience.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the ability to bear hardship over time, a close synonym of patience.

clue.text: He would probably be expected to do a spell at the Treasury

definitions.text: He would probably be expected to do a spell at the Treasury

parts.words: do a spell at the Treasury
parts.note: surface reading: someone serving a term of work in the government finance department
setter's reading: a magician casts spells, so this is a magician whose talent is with money

explanation.walkthrough: A spell is both a stint of duty and a magic charm, so the money expert at the Treasury is also a conjuror.
explanation.definitionFit: A financial wizard is a person with a near-magical skill for handling money and economics.

clue.text: When to keep quiet about waistband

indicators.note: about means around, so the call for quiet wraps round the other piece

parts.note: sh is the hushing sound asking for silence
as in 'as I arrived', meaning when

explanation.surface: A question about when to stay silent concerning a belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a broad strip of cloth worn around the waist as a band or belt.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lower in rank, a junior

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one complaint about an underling's work, but each half is a separate sense of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both lower in rank (a noun or adjective for a junior) and of lesser quality.

clue.text: Vent anger at having to take leading role

definitions.text: Vent anger at having to take leading role

parts.words: Vent anger at having to take leading role
parts.note: surface reading: an actor storms about being made the lead
setter's reading: the lead role of Shakespeare's revenge tragedy is spent venting anger at being made to avenge his father

explanation.walkthrough: The Danish prince curses the duty forced on him ('that ever I was born to set it right'), so an actor in that role vents anger at having to take the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking the title role of Shakespeare's tragedy means playing the prince who rails against his fate.

clue.text: Sporting club for insect and flying mammal

parts.note: a cricket is a chirping insect
the bat is the only mammal capable of true flight

explanation.surface: A sports association takes in a bug and a bat as members.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket bat is the wooden club used to strike the ball in the sport of cricket.

parts.note: surface reading: guns with a short range
setter's reading: a person with stubby limbs cannot reach far

explanation.walkthrough: Arms are both weapons and limbs; short limbs give a limited reach.
explanation.definitionFit: Small arms are firearms carried and fired by one person, such as pistols and rifles.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: something or someone that stretches
second meaning: in bricklaying, a brick laid lengthwise along the wall

explanation.walkthrough: 'Brick' also means a good-hearted person, which fits someone who reaches out; here it is the builder's term.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher is a brick laid with its long face showing, and literally something that stretches.

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word for party is read from right to left

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

indicators.note: about suggests turning things round, so the letters of one are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A group of theatregoers heads home, round about one in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Odeon is the name of a cinema chain and a classical word for a building for performances, so a theatre.

parts.note: RU is the abbreviation for Rugby Union
a sty is a pen for pigs

explanation.surface: A worn-out enclosure for playing in, eaten away by rust.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'game-pen' tempts you to look for a single thing such as a playpen; it is two pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Iron that has been corroded by air and water is covered in rust.

parts.note: the spruce is a conifer
S abbreviates Sabbath, as in Sun.

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up a tree in time for the day of rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To spruce up is to make neat and trim, so the verb means smartens.

clue.text: Work together with casemaker at one point

parts.note: a cooper makes casks and barrels, a kind of case
taken as written
E (east) is one of the four points of the compass

explanation.surface: Collaborating with a box-maker at a particular moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To cooperate is to act jointly with others toward a shared goal.

indicators.note: order as a verb tells you to arrange those two short words afresh

parts.note: ale is beer
the letters of these two words, rearranged

explanation.surface: At the pub, a drink if we decide to order the fish course.
explanation.definitionFit: The alewife is a North American herring-like fish.

clue.text: Indicate danger of rate change about that time

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for that time goes round the other letters
change tells you to alter the order of the letters of rate

parts.note: the four letters of rate, rearranged
then means at that time

explanation.surface: A warning that interest rates might move around that date.
explanation.definitionFit: Clouds that threaten rain are a sign that something bad is coming, so the verb means to signal danger.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a hill or mountain, as in South African place names and the German word
second meaning: Alban ..., the Austrian composer of the opera Wozzeck

explanation.walkthrough: Alfred Hill was an Australian composer, so a Canberra reader may take 'Hill the composer' as one person; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a hill or mountain in South African usage, and is also the surname of a twentieth-century Viennese composer.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small spotted carnivore related to the civet
second meaning: Jean ..., the French playwright and novelist

explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal writer' looks like an author of nature books; each word separately defines the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A genet is a catlike mammal of Africa and Europe, and Genet is the surname of a French author.

indicators.note: choice of says a selection is picked out from the words that come before

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A golfing team that can use just one club.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is a golf club with a metal head, used for shorter shots.

indicators.note: derived from says the letters are drawn straight out of the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A musical instrument that developed out of an early woodwind.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyre is an ancient stringed instrument, a small harp.

parts.note: the huckleberry is a small dark North American berry
a Finn is a native of Finland

explanation.surface: An unusual fruit being exported to someone in Scandinavia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective meaning new, describing the fruit; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Huckleberry Finn is the title of Mark Twain's 1884 novel about a boy rafting down the Mississippi.

clue.text: Make fresh adjustment in bizarre setting

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Something needs tweaking again because it was placed in a strange spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To reset something is to set or adjust it again, such as a clock or a broken bone.

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as in tendering a resignation
the superlative ending meaning most, as in kindest

explanation.surface: The kindest bid is the one made right at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works loosely: 'Most' does double duty, defining with 'considerate' and supplying the superlative ending, while 'at outset' says the word for offer goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tender means gentle and caring, so its superlative describes the most caring or thoughtful.
